description: Fireline Atlas is a solo project building a web app that combines NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into a map and daily calendar. The goal is to make it easier to explore where and when hotspots are detected. I’m developing the project with Python and web technologies for the MODIS and VIIRS hotspot harmonization challenge.
summary: Fireline Atlas is a web app for exploring NASA FIRMS active-fire detections from the MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors. Users can load recent FIRMS data with a map key or upload sensor CSV files, then filter by date, sensor, or area. A global map and daily hotspot calendar show where and when thermal anomalies were detected. For historical context, the app compares each sensor with its own same-date records from the previous year and, when data is available, an average from up to five earlier years. Separate sensor views help avoid treating MODIS and VIIRS counts as interchangeable because their spatial resolutions differ. Plain-language guidance explains what a hotspot can and cannot tell us, and the app credits NASA FIRMS.
details:
Fireline Atlas is a web app for exploring NASA FIRMS active-fire and thermal-anomaly observations from MODIS and VIIRS. Users can load recent data with a FIRMS map key or upload CSV files, choose the whole globe or a coordinate-based area, and filter by sensor and date. An interactive globe displays detections, while a daily calendar shows MODIS and VIIRS counts separately. Users can compare a selected date window with the same dates last year or with up to five earlier years when data is available, then inspect and download filtered records. The app makes fire-observation patterns easier to explore. Because the sensors have different pixel sizes, the app keeps their counts separate. A hotspot indicates unusual heat detected during a satellite overpass; it does not confirm a wildfire, show a fire perimeter, or predict fire spread. The app uses Python, Streamlit, pandas, Plotly, and NASA FIRMS data.

I used SI for ideation and brainstorming.
